summary: Near-real-time activity mirror to customer's S3 with per-event redaction policy and delivery proof
description: Customer requests a near-real-time mirror of Redwood audit events (authentication, request metadata, model invocation events, and per-request policy decisions) to their S3 bucket for regulatory retention and live SIEM ingestion. Requirements: 1) per-event redaction rules configurable by field and by event-type (customer-specified allowlist/denylist); 2) resume tokens and hour-by-hour manifest for resumable replay; 3) tamper-evidence: per-batch SHA-256 chain linking event IDs; 4) optional reversible pseudonymization for PII fields using customer-provided HSM key material (BYOK) with rotation policy; 5) retention and legal-hold tag support in object metadata; 6) delivery-heartbeat (every 5 minutes) to a monitoring endpoint and S3 delivery confirmations with timestamps. Customer expects a sample configuration, a runbook for audit, and evidence they can present to auditors (manifest + signature + sample replay).
steps_to_validate: 1) Provision an S3 bucket (customer) with a write policy and provide ARN+kms-key-alias
2) We configure a delivery connector in the customer's org that streams audit events to the bucket using envelope encryption
3) Validate manifest files appear in s3://<bucket>/manifests/YYYY/MM/DD/HH-manifest.json every hour
4) Confirm per-event redaction is applied by pulling sample event file and verifying allowlist fields are present and PII fields are pseudonymized
5) Test resumable replay by deleting last manifest and using resume token to request replay from Redwood API
6) Verify tamper-evidence by computing SHA-256 chain across returned event IDs and comparing to manifest chain
7) Confirm delivery-heartbeat POSTs to provided monitoring endpoint and S3 object metadata contains legal-hold tags
logs: Customer provided sample event bundle (attached in ticket) and an S3 policy snippet. Ingestion errors seen in last 24h: 3 transient 5xx write failures (internal transient), 1 access denied when trying a test with wrong KMS alias. See attached structured-log.txt
